lyrics:
[Intro: jerking sequencer line, drum machine, static]

[Verse 1: distorted rasping male voice, fragments]
I typed a word
It gave me another
I said a thing
It sounded like my brother

[Chorus: barked, metallic hits]
Autocorrect me
Did you mean, did you mean
Autocorrect me
Smooth and clean
Take the edges, take the spelling
Autocorrect me

[Verse 2: voice breaking up, sequencer doubling]
My name comes back
Underlined in red
The right one's what it gives me
The wrong one's in my head

[Chorus: barked, metallic hits]
Autocorrect me
Did you mean, did you mean
Autocorrect me
Smooth and clean
Take the edges, take the spelling
Autocorrect me

[Breakdown: sequencer alone, clean synthetic voice]
Did you mean: yes.
Did you mean: fine.
Did you mean: yes.

[Final Chorus: harshest, voice glitching, last line clean]
Autocorrect me
Did you mean, did you mean
Autocorrect me
Smooth and clean
Take the edges, take the spelling
No. I meant what I said.

[Outro: sequencer stutters, static, stops]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 124 BPM, 4/4, C minor. Jerking, harsh and danceable, like a machine with a limp.

VOICE: Male, heavily distorted into a dry rasp, delivered in short fragments, barked in the choruses and glitching apart near the end. A clean synthetic voice makes three suggestions in the breakdown. The final line is his own voice with no effect.

INSTRUMENTS: A hard, syncopated analogue sequencer line, a drum machine with a metallic snare, sampled metal hits, a low drone, bursts of static, a detuned lead that slides between notes, tape-stutter effects.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, sequencer and static. 0:16 Verse 1. 0:40 Chorus 1. 1:04 Verse 2. 1:28 Chorus 2. 1:52 Breakdown, the clean voice. 2:14 Final chorus, ending clean. 2:48 Outro, stutter and stop at 3:16.

PRODUCTION & MIX: 1985 industrial: raw, lo-fi and abrasive, cheap samplers and analogue sequencers, the voice more texture than words.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The undistorted 'No. I meant what I said.' at 2:42.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original's order to conform comes from outside and above. Now it arrives as a helpful suggestion under every word a person types, and resisting means insisting on a mistake.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Confused, eroded, nearly erased, himself.
